scope: Complete explicit sufficient conditions for every complex dimension n>=2: one cuspidally pinched square elliptic factor times n-1 square elliptic factors, an ambient-positive genuinely nonclosed surface-supported background, explicit positive reference repair, full-variable positive H^s data in a normalized perturbative ball, and the entire bounded canonical ordinary type. Fixed finite mass, constant-difference uniqueness against every rough competitor, actual disk and compact-fiber descent, ambient Holder 1/3 continuity, exact degree/Jacobian normalization and all-resolution/common-refinement independence. General P23 remains open.
status: Accepted, mathematically assessed, compiled and visually inspected; publication pending.

immutable_source_check.report: The exact premises follow from [Bedford–Taylor (1982)](https://www.math.stonybrook.edu/~ebedford/PapersForM655/BTNewCapacity.pdf), Theorems 2.1, 2.4 and 6.9, respectively. Theorem 2.4 includes canonical bounded psh weights and top-degree products. For premise 2, Definition 3.1 and Theorem 6.9 give zero mass for bounded psh Monge–Ampère measures on pluripolar sets. Locally set s=Σb_ℓ+|z|²; positivity bounds the stated mixed measure by ((d−r)!/d!)(dd^cs)^d. Shift/rescale s into the capacity’s unit interval and use a countable ball cover. Rescaling the source’s dd^c by 1/(4π) preserves all conclusions. The local bounded psh shifts fit these inputs. This audit leaves the separate n1/n2 hypotheses conditional.

passages.statement: Let D⊂C^d be open and 1≤r≤d. For each ℓ=1,…,r, let b_{ℓ,j} be locally uniformly bounded plurisubharmonic functions decreasing to a locally bounded canonical plurisubharmonic function b_ℓ. Then the Bedford–Taylor mixed currents dd^c b_{1,j}∧⋯∧dd^c b_{r,j} converge weakly on compact subsets to dd^c b_1∧⋯∧dd^c b_r, with dd^c=(i/(2π))∂bar∂.

Let D⊂C^d be open and 1≤r≤d. Let a_j and b_{1,j},…,b_{r,j} be locally uniformly bounded decreasing sequences of plurisubharmonic functions, with locally bounded canonical limits a and b_1,…,b_r. Multiplication uses these canonical Borel representatives. Then the weighted Bedford–Taylor currents a_j dd^c b_{1,j}∧⋯∧dd^c b_{r,j} converge weakly on compact subsets to a dd^c b_1∧⋯∧dd^c b_r, where dd^c=(i/(2π))∂bar∂.

Let D⊂C^d be open, let 1≤r≤d, and let b_1,…,b_r be locally bounded plurisubharmonic functions. Set β=dd^c|z|^2, with dd^c=(i/(2π))∂bar∂. The positive Bedford–Taylor measure dd^c b_1∧⋯∧dd^c b_r∧β^{d-r} gives zero mass to every locally pluripolar Borel subset of D.

Bedford–Taylor, Acta Mathematica 149 (1982), uses D=2i∂bar∂. On an open set Ω⊂C^n, mixed products of locally bounded plurisubharmonic functions are defined recursively by T(v_1,…,v_k)=D(v_1T(v_2,…,v_k)), T()=1. primary_sources.previous_unchanged_primary_reuse: Entire Section 6, including the full capacity-zero/pluripolar equivalence proof 6.9, root-read earlier for P20 ideal assessment. Definition 3.1 and Proposition 3.2 full statements/proof read in the current text extract.
primary_sources.application: Locally uniformly bounded canonical decreasing psh functions are obtained from the torus convolutions by fixed quadratic shifts and the same vanishing constants. Weighted convergence is also reconstructed independently by public n5 via the circular lift. Capacity zero and normalized bounded local psh sums give noncharging for every bounded background-corrected product.

Proposition 2.3 proves locally uniform convergence for continuous potentials; it does not prove arbitrary bounded decreasing continuity. Corollary 2.5 concerns analytic sets for continuous potentials. Full bounded decreasing and pluripolar conclusions use the separately checked 1982 source.
primary_sources.normalization: Source dd^c=2i partial barpartial is 4 pi times this paper convention. A degree-r product scales by (4 pi)^(-r); the smooth top product here is n! pi^(-n) det(u_jk) dLeb.

Bedford–Taylor, Acta Mathematica 149 (1982), uses D=2i∂bar∂. On an open set Ω⊂C^n, mixed products of locally bounded plurisubharmonic functions are defined recursively by T(v_1,…,v_k)=D(v_1T(v_2,…,v_k)), T()=1. They are positive closed currents and are symmetric and multilinear in their differentiated factors. Theorem 2.1 and Corollary 2.2 assert that, for 1≤k≤n, if v_j^i and v^i are locally bounded plurisubharmonic functions on Ω and v_j^i decreases pointwise to v^i for every i=1,…,k, then Dv_j^1∧⋯∧Dv_j^k converges weakly as currents to Dv^1∧⋯∧Dv^k.

Bedford–Taylor, Acta Mathematica 149 (1982), Definition 3.1 and Theorem 6.9, identify pluripolar sets with sets of zero outer capacity; in particular every pluripolar Borel set E⊂Ω has C_Ω^*(E)=0.

root_math_assessment: The finite degree-one cusp normalization is a homeomorphism and every disk lifts by bounded removable extension of y/x. A Fourier primitive repairs the rank-deficient pullback to a positive form. Surface-supported torsion annihilates dk wedge dc k, giving dd^c closure of every power and every mixed energy factor in every dimension. Explicit inverse and Sobolev polynomial estimates solve the full-variable nonlinear equation in a normalized positive density ball. Canonical decreasing convolutions, full weighted product convergence, uniform smooth coefficient limits and the flat energy inequality compare every bounded competitor with the positive constructed solution. All bounded masses are fixed by distributional Stokes. Borel pushforward injectivity gives the exact downstairs equation, the global regular-locus density is f/J with J=H^n/Omega, and lambda*f/rho is confined to the cusp chart. Actual disk descent, ambient Holder 1/3 continuity, literal compact-fiber constancy and noncharging of exceptional sets prove independence under every refinement. No arbitrary-space or pole-type classification is claimed.
